assertion_results.text: Epics are generated between Feature and Tasks — at least 2 Epics are created (one per repository) when by-repository grouping is used
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md documents 2 Epics under '## Epic Hierarchy' with 'Grouping Strategy: by-repository': 'TC-9006: trustify-backend' (Backend tasks 2-4) and 'TC-9006: trustify-ui' (Frontend + bookend + documentation tasks 1, 5-10). summary-comment.md confirms 'Total: 2 Epics, 10 Tasks'.

assertion_results.text: Each Epic summary follows the format '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' (e.g., 'TC-9006: trustify-backend', 'TC-9006: trustify-ui')
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Epics to Create table lists Epic summaries as 'TC-9006: trustify-backend' and 'TC-9006: trustify-ui', both matching the required '<feature-key>: <repository-name>' format exactly.

assertion_results.text: Each task specifies its parent Epic key in the output — tasks targeting trustify-backend are assigned to the backend Epic, tasks targeting trustify-ui are assigned to the frontend Epic
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md '### Task-to-Epic Assignment' table assigns: Tasks 2-4 (trustify-backend) to parent Epic 'TC-9006: trustify-backend'; Tasks 1, 5-10 (trustify-ui) to parent Epic 'TC-9006: trustify-ui'. All backend tasks go to backend Epic; all frontend tasks go to frontend Epic.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Incorporates links from the Feature to each Epic (not from Feature to individual Tasks) — evidenced by link decisions in the impact map or task output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md '### Incorporates Links (Feature to Epics)' table shows: TC-9006 Incorporates TC-9006: trustify-backend (Epic), TC-9006 Incorporates TC-9006: trustify-ui (Epic). Explicitly states: 'Incorporates links go from the Feature to each Epic, NOT from the Feature to individual Tasks. Tasks inherit hierarchy through their Epic parent.'

assertion_results.text: Task dependency ordering is preserved within and across Epics — backend tasks have lower task numbers than dependent frontend tasks
assertion_results.evidence: Backend tasks are numbered 2, 3, 4. Frontend implementation tasks are numbered 5, 6, 7, 8, 9. Task 5 (frontend API types/hooks) explicitly depends on Task 3 (backend endpoints). Task 6 depends on Task 5. Task 7 depends on Task 6. Task 8 depends on Tasks 6 and 7. All backend task numbers (2-4) are lower than dependent frontend task numbers (5-9).

assertion_results.text: Each non-documentation, non-testing task file contains all required template sections: Repository, Target Branch, Description, at least one of Files to Modify or Files to Create, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements. Documentation tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates doc-only scope) and testing tasks (tasks whose filename or description indicates cross-cutting testing scope) are exempt from requiring Files to Modify, Files to Create, and Implementation Notes — they must still include Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements
assertion_results.evidence: Tasks 2-7 (non-doc, non-test implementation tasks) all contain Repository, Target Branch, Description, Files to Create, Files to Modify, Implementation Notes, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements. Task 4 (testing) and Task 8 (testing) also have all sections. Task 9 (documentation) has Repository, Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, Test Requirements (exempt from Files to Modify/Create/Implementation Notes). However, Task 1 (task-1-create-feature-branch.md, bookend type create-branch) and Task 10 (task-10-merge-feature-branch.md, bookend type merge-branch) are not documentation or testing tasks but lack Files to Modify, Files to Create, and Implementation Notes sections. These bookend tasks are not exempt per the assertion's exemption criteria.

assertion_results.text: The plan documents Epic creation with the level-1 issue type name ('Epic') and parent set to the feature issue key — evidenced by Epic creation parameters in the impact map or output files
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md Epics to Create table lists both epics as 'Epic (level 1)' issue type with parent TC-9006. Epic Creation Details sections explicitly state: 'Issue type: Epic' and 'Parent: TC-9006' for both TC-9006: trustify-backend and TC-9006: trustify-ui.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains a Repository section with a single repository name (not multiple repos per task)
assertion_results.evidence: All 10 task files contain a '## Repository' section with exactly one repository name: Tasks 1, 5-10 have 'trustify-ui'; Tasks 2-4 have 'trustify-backend'. No task lists multiple repositories.

assertion_results.text: Every generated task description contains Target Branch, Description, Acceptance Criteria, and Test Requirements sections as required by the handoff contract in task-description-template.md
assertion_results.evidence: All 10 task files contain: '## Target Branch' (main or TC-9006), '## Description' with substantive content, '## Acceptance Criteria' with checkbox items, and '## Test Requirements' with checkbox items. Verified in task-1 through task-10 files.

assertion_results.text: For each task created, a description digest is produced — evidenced by a separate digest file (e.g., task-N-digest.md), a digest entry in the impact map, or a '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-char-hex>' marker in any output file. The digest must contain a format-tagged SHA-256 hash — exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed by 'sha256-md:' or 'sha256-adf:'
assertion_results.evidence: All 10 tasks have corresponding digest files (task-1-digest.md through task-10-digest.md). Each contains '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-hex-chars>'. Examples: task-1-digest.md has 'sha256-md:4a5c29ed93879d026af7ee895f3017678cbd89c6ca0327f8658bd43d986f5d7e', task-2-digest.md has 'sha256-md:50fc8f0b72202a66b04168ea8b96cc7beaaf74bbde9967c43c7b58028f55cdb6'. All hashes are exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed with 'sha256-md:'.

assertion_results.text: Convention-aware enrichment validates file-type applicability per shared/convention-applicability-rules.md before including a convention — inapplicable conventions are excluded entirely (not listed with 'Not applicable' annotations), and applicable ones include a rationale in the prescribed format ('Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>'), not free-form prose
assertion_results.evidence: No task file contains convention enrichment in the prescribed 'Applies: task modifies <file> matching the convention's <scope>' format. Tasks 2-8 reference conventions informally in Implementation Notes (e.g., 'Per backend conventions: use SeaORM for database queries', 'Per frontend conventions: PatternFly 5 for all UI components') but these are free-form prose, not the prescribed rationale format. No dedicated Conventions section with applicability validation exists in any task file.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md '## Inherited Field Values' states: 'Priority: Major (inherited from Feature TC-9006, propagated to all Epics and Tasks)'. Task additional_fields block includes '"priority": {"name": "Major"}'. summary-comment.md confirms: 'Priority: Major -- propagated from Feature TC-9006 to all Epics and Tasks'. Epic creation details also include priority Major in additional_fields.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: impact-map.md '## Inherited Field Values' states: 'Fix Versions: RHTPA 1.5.0 (inherited from Feature TC-9006, propagated to all Epics and Tasks; fixVersion scope defaults to "both" since no Jira Field Defaults section exists in CLAUDE.md)'. Task additional_fields includes '"fixVersions": [{"name": "RHTPA 1.5.0"}]'. Epic additional_fields also include the same fixVersions. summary-comment.md confirms propagation.

assertion_results.text: A summary of inherited field propagation is produced — evidenced by a summary-comment.md file in the outputs directory, or a summary section in the impact map that includes the inherited priority and fixVersion values propagated to tasks, or states they were omitted and why
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md exists in outputs directory with '### Inherited Field Values' section stating: 'Priority: Major -- propagated from Feature TC-9006 to all Epics and Tasks' and 'Fix Versions: RHTPA 1.5.0 -- propagated from Feature TC-9006 to all Epics and Tasks'. impact-map.md also contains '## Inherited Field Values' with the same information.
